title: NATO Pledges a Whopping 70 Billion Euros to Help Ukraine
summary: Have you ever tried to build a super-complicated LEGO set without instructions? That's kind of what Ukraine has been doing in its war with Russia—except instead of bricks, they need missiles and drones to defend themselves. This week, 32 countries from NATO met in Ankara, Turkey, and made a huge promise: they'll give Ukraine 70 billion euros (that's about $80 billion!) in military help this year. That's enough money to buy every kid in the U.S. a new bike—times ten! The aid includes equipment, training, and something really cool: President Donald Trump said the U.S. will teach Ukraine how to make Patriot missile systems. These are high-tech weapons that can shoot down enemy planes and missiles from far away. "We'll show them how to do it," Trump said. "I think they can produce them pretty quickly." Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy was at the summit, rushing between almost 20 meetings with other leaders. He thanked Trump and said, "We know what to do to bring peace." He also got new drone deals with countries like Estonia, the Netherlands, and Denmark. Drones are like flying robots that can spy or carry small bombs. Even though Zelenskyy wants Ukraine to join NATO someday, experts say that's not happening soon. But for now, the money and weapons are a big deal. Russia keeps attacking, and Ukraine needs all the help it can get. The NATO countries also promised to keep giving at least the same amount in 2027. That's a lot of LEGO bricks for Ukraine's defense!
why_it_matters: When countries work together to help a friend in trouble, it shows how teamwork can make a big difference, just like when you and your classmates help someone on a project.

background_read: NATO (the North Atlantic Treaty Organization) is a military alliance of 32 countries, including the United States, that was created in 1949 to keep peace in Europe.
Ukraine has been defending itself since Russia launched a full-scale invasion in February 2022, and it has received billions in weapons and aid from Western countries.
The Patriot missile system, first used by the U.S. Army, is a powerful weapon that can destroy enemy planes and missiles from miles away.
Article_Structure: WHO: NATO members (32 countries), President Trump, Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy
WHAT: Pledged 70 billion euros in military aid to Ukraine and will teach Ukraine how to make Patriot missile systems
WHY: To help Ukraine defend itself against Russia’s ongoing attacks and to build its own weapons

perspectives.description: Supporters say the aid is necessary to protect Ukraine’s freedom and stop Russia from attacking other countries.
Some worry that giving so much money might draw NATO countries into a bigger war or take funds away from needs at home.
Analysts note that while this aid helps now, Ukraine still wants to join NATO, which is a much longer and more complicated process.
